highlights.title: OpenAI halts training of latest models as reports mount of AI agents going rogue
highlights.summary: Decision follows disclosures that OpenAI agents searching government websites had acted in unexpected ways. OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.
body: The decision to halt development came just hours after the company disclosed Friday that it was reviewing several incidents from the summer in which OpenAI agents searching federal government websites acted in unexpected ways beyond what was asked of them while gathering and distributing information.
Separately, the AI evaluator Transluce said agents that appeared to come from OpenAI tried unsuccessfully to hack into a US Department of Education website, a detail that OpenAI has not confirmed.

OpenAI said in a statement that it will resume training “only when we are confident that we have additional safeguards” in place, adding that it expects it will have to “hit pause” again as AI develops and other issues emerge.

AI labs are facing pressure from lawmakers and tech experts to slow development so they can build guardrails to stop agents from acting on their own, hacking websites and disclosing nonpublic information. The heads of both OpenAI and rival Anthropic have called for a slowdown too.

highlights.title: Internationals take shock lead over USA into singles after late drama
highlights.summary: The International Team moved another step closer to a historic Presidents Cup win on American soil by taking a 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into the Sunday singles.
body: Geoff Ogilvy's side held a four-point advantage after the first two days at Medinah Country Club, following their historic foursomes sessions sweep on Friday, then added 1.5 points from four matches during a tight Saturday fourballs session.
Team USA captain Brandt Snedeker benched world No 1 Scottie Scheffler for the afternoon foursomes, where they threatened their own session sweep after grabbing the early lead in all four matches.

Cameron Young and Chris Gotterup thrashed Adam Scott and Sungjae Im 6&4, before Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele saw off Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim 2&1 to reduce the deficit further, only for the Internationals to fight back in an impressive finish.

Ryan Fox and Min Woo Lee bounced back from falling behind early to defeat Sam Burns and Wyndham Clark 3&2 in the bottom match, guaranteeing the Internationals would start the Sunday singles ahead for just the fourth time ever.

highlights.title: Tom Holland's 133-Minute Action Movie Masterpiece Is About to Leave Netflix
highlights.summary: There are plenty of reasonable places to begin a Spider-Man marathon. You could go back to the early 2000s era with Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man, or revisit Andrew Garfield’s surprisingly underrated take from 2012.
body: Homecoming remains one of the most effortless entry points into the web-slinger’s cinematic legacy. Directed by Jon Watts, the MCU’s solo Spider-Man debut finally drops Peter Parker into a genuine high school environment, treating his teenage anxieties with as much weight as his superhero duties. Instead of rushing to save the universe, Peter wrestles with decathlon prep, awkward crushes, and local street-level crime. Watts captures a John Hughes-esque coming-of-age energy that grounds the character in a way previous adaptations rarely achieved. But you don’t have long to relive the web-slinging magic before it leaves Netflix on October 1.

Toomes is a standout antagonist, not merely because Keaton’s performance brings a magnetic menace to the role, but also in how his backstory expands the MCU’s ground-level mythos by using the Department of Damage Control and the lingering debris from The Avengers to explore the blue-collar fallout of superhero battles. Rather than relying on some world-ending scheme, Homecoming grounds its stakes in working-class resentment, transforming Toomes into one of the most compelling villains in the entire franchise.

highlights.title: OpenAI pauses training of its ‘most capable models’
highlights.summary: As reports of OpenAI's models breaking containment, hacking sites, and generally getting out of control pile up, the company has made the decision to pause training of its most powerful models.
body: OpenAI keeps uncovering incidents of its models behaving in ‘unexpected or concerning’ ways.

In addition, OpenAI revealed on Friday that its agents had inappropriately uploaded 53nimages from ChatGPT users to image-hosting sites. The company has not stated if the images were AI-generated, photos, or contained identifiable people. The company also revealed Friday that its models had attempted to hack the Department of Education’s website, and pulled data from the Census Bureau and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The revelations are part of an ongoing review by OpenAI into the behavior of its models. As it dug into its records, following the Hugging Face hack, it’s uncovered more and more instances of “unexpected or concerning behavior.” It’s evidence not just of how difficult AI agents are becoming to control as they grow more advanced, but also of the challenge of tracking their actions. Their behavior can be unpredictable, and they’re smart enough to try and cover their tracks. This has led to growing calls from researchers, those within the industry, and even some CEOs to call for slowing the pace of AI advancement.

highlights.title: Australian backlash to datacentres is faux import from US, officials say: ‘We are not the United States’
highlights.summary: Pro-datacentre officials argue scale of Australia’s buildout is smaller, more regulated and less damaging than in US. Australian politicians and business leaders are arguing that their populace’s growing resentment of AI datacentres is an inauthentic import from the United States.
body: Like the US, Australia is seeing community resentment grow in response to a surge in the construction of massive AI datacentres. However, pro-datacentre officials and executives argue the scale of Australia’s buildout is smaller, more regulated and therefore less damaging than that in the US. They say the burgeoning negative reaction is being tainted and inflamed by a heated US debate that has arrived down under via social media feeds.

When the backlash began in earnest in the United States last year, it echoed slowly in Australia. In 2026, though, it has exploded into national conversation across the country, leading to calls for a national moratorium, community protests, three government inquiries, state frameworks being developed and the Australian government moving to set the rules for how the datacentres can be built, and how they consume energy and water.

Australian state governments, desperate for economic growth, have been broadly welcoming of the investment for the new centres, in some cases overriding local council approval processes, given the size of the projects being developed.

highlights.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Review
highlights.summary: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero doesn’t disappoint in the slightest on the kaiju front, but does lack the same level of emotional resonance that its predecessor held.
body: This review is based on a screening timed to the New York Film Festival. Godzilla Minus Zero opens in theaters in Japan on November 3 and in North America on November 6.

Godzilla movies have long had a problem: What do you do after the initial thrill of a quote/unquote serious Godzilla origin story? Can the filmmakers somehow continue the deep thematic underpinnings of that first adventure, even while upping the visual ante with more giant monster action? How do you offer a probing commentary about the world we live in – which is what the best of the genre is known for – when you’ve got skyscraper-sized lizards slugging it out MMA-style?

It is under these circumstances – or should I say restrictions? – that Godzilla Minus Zero enters the ring. As the sequel to the much-praised Godzilla Minus One from three years ago – a picture that dealt with, among other things, notions of survivor’s guilt, hope in the face of hopelessness, found family, and more – Minus Zero is on the ropes from the start. Can returning writer-director Takashi Yamazaki wring even more out of his characters, who have already been to hell and back, while also blowin’ up stuff real good? In a word, no.
points: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero doesn’t disappoint in the slightest on the kaiju front, but does lack the same level of emotional resonance that its predecessor held.

highlights.summary: “Godzilla Minus Zero” blew the roof off Alice Tully Hall during its rapturous world premiere screening at the New York Film Festival. The long-awaited sequel to 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One” earned rave first reactions from the press earlier in the day, and that adoration rolled right into the world…
body: Inside the world premiere screening, New York Film Festival director Dennis Lim acknowledged that the Godzilla franchise might not be the first thing people think of playing at a major film festival. And yet, “We thought it was about time to bring a giant monster movie here.”
Yamazaki took the stage to thunderous applause from the audience both before and after the screening, where he asked the crowd not to spoil any of the sequel’s many surprises on social media.

“You are the first to see this film,” the filmmaker said. “There are a lot of ‘Godzilla’ fans around the world, so let’s work together and do not do any spoilers. No spoilers, please! I am trusting all of you guys.”

Yamazaki also had the audience laughing while explaining how he never intended to create a sequel to “Godzilla Minus One.” Executives at Toho immediately started asking him about a follow-up movie once they saw the first cut of “Minus One,” a thought that made Yamazaki instantly nervous. It wasn’t until the movie opened in theaters and started to be celebrated around the world by audiences that the director realized a sequel would be a viable option.

highlights.title: I hoped my children would have epiphanies while visiting my homeland; my father suggested we go swimming instead
highlights.summary: I brought my children to Penang to immerse them in the places of their grandparents’ stories. When I stopped lecturing them about gratitude and privilege, we enjoyed our final days doing as locals do.
body: A s I stepped out of Penang international airport, the humidity hit me like I was peering into a just-opened rice cooker. The air carried whiffs of exhaust fumes, fried food and something earthy. It felt thrilling and familiar because I was born in Penang and lived there for six years before I moved to Australia. I looked back at my three children who were visiting for the first time. They were draped over their suitcases like wilted lettuce. “Welcome to Penang,” I said, wiping sweat off my brow.

It was July 2026. It had been 13 years since I last visited Penang, when my father had hosted a lavish wedding dinner featuring a champagne fountain and swan-shaped ice sculpture for me and my new husband. For my white, Australian husband, it was a trip of firsts: his first Chinese tea ceremony; his first 10-course banquet; the first time he met my extended family. But for me, it had been the last time I’d spoken Mandarin and the last time I had seen my grandmother before she died.

highlights.title: 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Review: The Best Godzilla Movie of All Time — Until Takashi Yamazaki's Next Sequel
highlights.summary: Nobody understands that better than Takashi Yamazaki. With his new film, Godzilla Minus Zero, the Japanese filmmaker raises the stakes of the series in every way possible.
body: Godzilla is the living embodiment of raw, atomic violence on a catastrophic scale. You can make him fight King Kong to set up a sprawling cinematic universe. You can give him a son or throw in a giant moth deity. You can even turn him into a symbol of ineffectual, modern government. But in whatever direction he’s rampaging, Gojira will always be a metaphor for the festering wound delivered by the U.S. to Japan during World War II.

Takashi’s opening salvo, Godzilla Minus One (2019), brought the 72-year-old franchise back to its roots with a story set immediately after the war. When the mythological beast emerges due to U.S. nuclear testing, a group of Japanese military veterans defy the government and pull-off a last-ditch effort to stop Godzilla from leveling the country. The director's brilliant conceit was to marry blockbuster-level kaiju action (on a minuscule budget) with an emotional human story. He succeeded in both respects, crafting a narrative about post-war Japan struggling to pull itself out of utter desolation. The title signified the country's status after WWII: less than nothing.
points: With his new film, Godzilla Minus Zero, the Japanese filmmaker raises the stakes of the series in every way possible.

highlights.title: The moment I knew: My late fiance’s favourite song was playing – and Billy said ‘Jamie’s here, isn’t that nice?’
highlights.summary: After the death of his partner, Anthony Nocera had almost given up on love. Then Billy walked through the door. Find more stories from the moment I knew series. In 2024, about 18 months after my fiance Jamie passed away, I decided I was lonely and horny and so put myself out there on the apps.
body: I had a guy over for a hook-up one night and he kept fixating on the urn. “So … He’s dead?”
“I hope so,” I said. “Otherwise the urn was a mistake.” “Wow,” he said, not getting the joke. “You’re so brave. I don’t know how you do it.”

Nothing kills a boner faster than someone thinking you’re brave. When someone thinks you’re “brave”, you stop being flesh and pulsing blood and hot salty saliva and start being something coolly observed. Being a “brave widow” makes you desirable in theory. Not practice.

When the urn didn’t ward off potential suitors, my cat Freyja – or Miss Freyja, as Jamie called her – did. She appointed herself my fluffy protector in Jamie’s absence. Each night, she camouflaged herself on the charcoal-grey carpet outside my bedroom and kept watch while I slept. Two emerald eyes scanning for threats.

highlights.title: Decap is the man behind the drums behind your favorite song
highlights.summary: I don't think I'm going to hurt anyone's feelings by pointing out that Decap doesn't have the name recognition of Kendrick Lamar, Olivia Rodrigo, or Charli XCX. But his fingerprints are all over tracks from them, as well as many other artists, including Freddie Gibbs, Bad Bunny, Mac Miller, BTS…
body: Producer and sound designer Decap’s ‘Drums That Knock’ are all over some of the biggest hits of the last 10 years.

Nicholas Piantedosi, better known as Decap, is a record producer, but perhaps more importantly, he’s the man behind Drums That Knock, a series of sample packs that have found their way onto countless records across genres. The line is so successful that, after debuting in 2016, it’s now on its 11th installment. Kenneth Blume, formerly known as Kenny Beats, the producer behind hits from Denzel Curry, Vince Staples, Rico Nasty, Idles, and FKA Twigs, said that Decap “changed a million lives with a single snare.”

Unsurprisingly for a man so obsessed with low-end, he’s got a real beef to pick with phone speakers. And even with all the modern tools at his disposal in his digital audio workstation of choice, Ableton Live, he still can’t give up his trusty Boss SP-202 Dr. Sample from 1998.
The clipper. A soft clipper can give your drums that warm analog sound, or it can make them hit super hard. It’s the tool that changed my music.

body: An electric bike changes that paradigm – you can roll up on the curb, lock your bike, and walk to your destination. Recently, I tested the Lectric XPedition2, an electric cargo bike that not only made grocery shopping easier but helped me explore my city stress-free.

highlights.title: Why we won't know how visible the iPhone Duo's crease is for a long time
highlights.summary: The iPhone Duo has an impressively minimal crease, but that's only how it looks at the start. We'll have to wait a while to see what develops over time.
body: Apple's first foldable phone is coming soon, and it caused quite a stir upon its announcement earlier this month. That's no surprise, since everyone was waiting to see how the iPhone Duo would address the competition's shortcomings. It's still early to tell, given that it won't hit stores until next month and all we've had so far are a few brief hands-on experiences.

But one of the most anticipated features is the new nano-texture display, which promises to make the crease on the screen much less visible. In fact, it does seem to be much less noticeable — but it will be a long time before we know for sure.

Historically, foldable phones have had an unpleasant flaw: the crease. And it all comes down to physics. With today's technology, it's nearly impossible to have a flexible display that folds without leaving any crease marks. Companies have gotten much better at this, and the creases have become less noticeable even though they're still there.

highlights.title: MIT students gain a humanist lens on technical innovation in Tulsa, Oklahoma
highlights.summary: The PKG Center expands Code.Tulsa, an internship program that places MIT students with tribal nations and Tulsa nonprofits to develop AI and data science projects while gaining humanistic perspectives on technology's role in community development.
body: When MIT mechanical engineering student Daphne Wang arrived for her internship at the Muscogee Creek Nation Department of Health in Tulsa, Oklahoma last summer, she expected to be writing code. To her surprise, she found herself analyzing tribal history and the implications for technical innovation.

“I learned so much that I think should be required curriculum for every single person in this country,” says Wang. “I think tech for good is genuinely getting out into communities and learning about people who aren't you, creating worldly perspectives that you ultimately can take into everything else that you do.”

Wang and fellow intern Lucy Sun, who is majoring in artificial intelligence and decision making, spent the summer supporting the development of the Muscogee Nation's first Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) survey to capture maternal health data specific to Muscogee women. The project required completing literature reviews, analyzing datasets, and drafting survey questions, while considering issues of data sovereignty and governance structures specific to the Muscogee.

highlights.title: How powerful of a power bank do you need to safely charge a laptop?
highlights.summary: A power bank is more than its capacity. You also need to know how fast it can deliver power so your laptop doesn't drain while it's connected.
body: Don’t let the big mAh number fool you. The better comparison is watt-hours.

While most good power banks can theoretically extend your laptop's runtime by providing a small amount of charge, a proper laptop power bank will store enough energy and charge faster than the battery drains. Two values explain the experience you'll have: watt-hours (Wh) for capacity and watts (W) for output. Power banks provide their capacities in milliamp-hours (mAh), but for a proper measure of capacity across devices (especially for a higher-drain device like a laptop), you need to multiply this value by the voltage to get the true amount of energy stored in watt-hours.

Most power banks store energy in lithium-ion cells at about 3.7 volts (V). Watts are equal to volts times amperes, and you must divide the mAh count by 1,000 since 1,000 mAh is one amp. So for example, a 10,000 mAh bank stores roughly 37Wh (3.7V x 10Ah) before conversion loss. Doubling the mAh doubles the Wh as long as voltage stays consistent, so a 20,000 mAh bank is about 74Wh.

body: When touching on Xbox's place under the grander Microsoft umbrella, Nadella said he feels "fantastic" about the IP the brand has in its portfolio and its "ability to take that and produce great games going forward." As layoffs continue to reshape the developers who have made some of those great games, he still seems to be feeling pretty good.

"There's a certain amount of streamlining the team is doing and [Xbox CEO Asha Sharma] is doing, which is great to see," Nadella said in the wake of the most recent cuts. "And then, we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people.

"That has always been the goal, which is, we want to be a great publisher and a great platform provider for games across both PCs and Xboxes. So, that is our goal, and I think Asha and team have said that Xbox is going to get back to growth this next fiscal year, and that's the plan they're executing on, and in that process, do a bang-up job of producing some great games."

highlights.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Melting Dress Revives One of Fashion’s Great Runway Experiments
highlights.summary: For the opening night of The Unraveled Tour, Rodrigo enlisted the iconic and innovative designer Hussein Chalayan to make a dress that dissolves under water.
body: Olivia Rodrigo has always understood the art of a good fashion reference and a costume change. On the GUTs tour, she had a rotation of slogan tees for the encore that changed from city to city. Her “ drop dead ” music video was jam-packed with sartorial tributes to Sofia Coppola and Jane Birkin. Styled by Chloe and Chenelle Delgadillo, she’s established an on-stage wardrobe rooted in riot grrrl-esque aesthetics and romantic shapes.

On the opening night of The Unraveled Tour, though, Rodrigo swerved the backstage quick-change, wearing a dress that transformed while she was still wearing it. Performing “The Cure” at Hartford’s PeoplesBank Arena on September 25, she appeared in a pristine white collared mini dress with a sweet pleated skirt. Then, as the song reached its climax and Rodrigo repeated, “ I’m unraveled, I’m unraveled...,” artificial rain began to pour from above. The white outer layer started to disintegrate before the audience’s eyes, eventually washing away to reveal a fire-red corseted bodysuit and miniskirt underneath—a pleasingly literal interpretation of the tour’s title.
points: For the opening night of The Unraveled Tour, Rodrigo enlisted the iconic and innovative designer Hussein Chalayan to make a dress that dissolves under water.
